summary: Space Health Guardian (SHG V9.0) is a crew-centered spaceflight health intelligence and decision-support platform designed to address communication latency and fragmented telemetry during deep-space missions. Built with Python and Streamlit, SHG unifies 9 astronaut physiological metrics and spacecraft cabin environmental indicators into one interactive dashboard. Grounded in NASA Human Research Program (HRP), OSDR, and NLSP frameworks, the platform features automated range screening, multi-metric hazard correlations, a 7-region interactive body map, multi-crew digital twins, live microcontroller serial ingestion, and one-click handoff reports to assist astronauts and Earth-based flight surgeons
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Space Health Guardian (SHG V9.0) is an interactive, crew-centered spaceflight health intelligence and decision-support platform built for deep-space missions (Spacecraft, Space Stations, Lunar Bases, and Mars Habitats). It unifies 9 astronaut physiological metrics (Heart Rate, Systolic BP, SpO2, Respiratory Rate, Body Temperature, Sleep Duration, Activity Index) with cabin environmental metrics (Cabin CO2 and Radiation Dose) into one dashboard.

• Data Ingestion: It operates via three flexible pipelines: a Gaussian-distributed Synthetic Mission Simulator (SIMULATED DEMO), a Universal CSV Batch Importer (supporting Long and Wide formats), and a live USB/Serial hardware bridge (pyserial) for wearable microcontrollers.

• Automated Screening & Analytics: It evaluates metrics against configurable screening bands, performs automated physiological plausibility checks, computes rolling linear trend slopes, and maps multi-metric correlations.

• Preventive Care & Handoffs: It includes a 7-region interactive body map, multi-crew digital twins, an exam scheduler, a 7-domain prevention guide, and a one-click .txt flight-surgeon handoff generator.

2. Benefits & Expected Impact

During deep-space exploration, communication latency with Earth can reach up to 20+ minutes each way, making real-time ground monitoring impossible. SHG empowers astronauts with autonomous onboard screening tools to detect gradual physiological shifts early, correlate cabin air quality spikes with crew fatigue or SpO2 changes, and generate clear, structured handoff summaries for Earth-based flight surgeons. This reduces cognitive load on the crew and improves medical readiness in isolated environments.

3. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

• Programming Language & Frontend: Python 3, Streamlit, and Custom CSS (for a dark-mode, mission-control UI).

• Data Analytics & Visualization: Pandas, NumPy (for normalization, correlation matrices, and polyfit trend slopes), and Plotly Graph Objects (for interactive charts and heatmaps).

• Hardware Integration: PySerial and JSON protocols designed to ingest live telemetry from edge wearable microcontrollers such as Arduino and ESP32 at selectable baud rates (9600–115200).

• NASA Open Resources: Grounded in NASA Human Research Program (HRP) 5 Hazards taxonomy, NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), NASA Life Sciences Portal (NLSP), and NASA Open Data Portal.

4. Creativity & Innovation

• Multi-Crew Digital Twins: Allows side-by-side longitudinal comparison of unlimited crew profiles (Crew-01, Crew-02, etc.) across different mission habitats.

• Interactive 7-Region Body Map: Connects specific anatomical systems (e.g., Brain & Eyes for SANS, Heart & Lungs, Muscles & Bones) directly to spaceflight confounders and preventive actions.

• Responsible Gamification (XP System): Rewards consistent routine health logging (+10 XP per scheduled check) while strictly avoiding any incentives to ignore symptoms or override safety alerts.

5. Key Factors Considered by Our Team

• Clinical Safety & Non-Diagnostic Guardrails: Because SHG is an educational decision-support prototype and not a certified medical device, we implemented strict disclaimers, automated data-quality validation (SpO2 0–100%, Sleep ≤ 24h), and explicit separation between environmental indicators (Cabin CO2 in ppm) and clinical blood gas metrics—reminding users that correlation does not imply causation.

• Contextual Evaluation: Raw vital signs in space cannot be judged by Earth standards alone; therefore, our design accounts for microgravity fluid shifts, posture, workload, and mission environment baselines.
